user.title: Connect to your TP-Link router
user.description: Enter the router's IP address and the password you use for its web interface. Model detection can take up to a couple of minutes.

data_description.host: For example 192.168.0.1. Prefix with https:// if your router only serves HTTPS.
data_description.username: Most routers use 'admin'. Only change this if your router asks for a different username.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter router password
reauth_confirm.description: The router at {host} rejected the stored password.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the router. Check the IP address and that Home Assistant is on the same network.
error.login_failed: Login failed: either the password is wrong or this router model is not supported by tplinkrouterc6u. Also make sure nobody is logged into the router's web interface.
error.timeout: The router took too long to respond.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant logs.

init.title: TP-Link Router Care options
init.description:
The guest Wi-Fi QR card can also be fetched as a PNG from a webhook URL (local network only, no login needed). Add `?theme=light` or `?theme=dark` to override the card theme.

Webhook (currently {webhook_status}): `{webhook_url}`

data_description.qr_theme: Look of the Guest 5 GHz QR code image. The QR code itself stays dark-on-white in both themes so every phone can scan it.
data_description.webhook_enabled: Serve the QR card at the webhook URL. The card shows the guest password, so leave this off if you don't need it.
data_description.webhook_id: Last part of the webhook URL. Set your own fixed ID (letters, digits, - and _), or clear the field to generate a new random one. Anyone on your network who knows it can see the guest password, so use something hard to guess.

error.webhook_id_taken: Another integration already uses this webhook ID.
